title: Reduce deep-scroll tail latency by implementing async page reshaper and targeted prefetch
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Several customers and internal dashboards show large tail latencies (95th/99th) when users perform deep scrolls or jump to far offsets in time-series explorations. Investigation shows high read-amplification from scanning many small index segments and repeatedly rehydrating KV cursor state for adjacent pages. This manifests as timeouts, expensive retries, and a spike in RB latency for tenant-heavy queries.

Observations and telemetry: we see a cluster of tenants (top 2%) responsible for ~40% of long-tail page loads. Index scan time correlates with number of segment boundaries crossed and with scan fanout for sparse time ranges. Current stable-cursor pagination forces repeated seek+scan across small shards for each page boundary, and our read-through cache has low hit rates for wide-window jumps.

Goal: design and ship an "async page reshaper" backend component that reshapes paginated responses by performing prioritized background prefetch of adjacent pages and compact segment summaries, while preserving strong consistency and graceful fallbacks. Measurable targets: cut 99th-page-load latency by >=45% for deep scrolls and reduce read-amplification (I/O ops per page) by >=30% in canary tenants.
acceptance_criteria: 99th percentile page-load latency reduced by >=45% for synthetic deep-scroll workload on canary cluster
Prefetching is behind a feature flag; canary rollout able to be toggled per-tenant and instantly disabled to fallback to current pagination path
End-to-end integration tests and stress harness added to the perf repo, plus dashboards showing I/O ops per page and per-tenant prefetch hit rates
tasks: Instrument index scan traces: emit segment-cross counters and per-page I/O metrics (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12345)
Prototype async page reshaper service: prioritized prefetch queue, per-tenant memory budget, compact summary cache
Add bloom-time filters to segment metadata to cheaply skip segments with no relevant time ranges
Implement adaptive overscan policy: small tenants get minimal overscan, hot tenants get wider prefetch window
Create canary framework: per-tenant feature flags, canary rollout metric set and alerting
Add integration + stress tests in perf-harness with synthetic tenant workloads (deep-scroll, time-jump, mixed)
decisions: Design trade-off: keep prefetch strictly read-only and asynchronously merge into response; this avoids write amplification and simplifies rollback
Memory vs latency: we will enforce a per-tenant budget with LRU eviction for compact summaries to avoid noisy-neighbor OOMs
Consistency model: prefetch will only be used for non-real-time queries (>=5s query age) for first rollout; live queries will continue to use exact scan path to avoid staleness concerns
Fallback: if prefetch queue saturates or summary cache misses, system falls back to existing pagination path with no functional change
